final_prompt:
I want a habit tracker for personal use: just me, no accounts or login, with all data stored locally in the browser. Build it as a new small web app in a new folder, `habit-tracker/`, inside the current working directory. There is no existing code to touch. Nothing outside that folder should be created or changed.

Speed mode is MVP. Build the thinnest working slice. Throwaway structure is fine, so don't add abstractions, and don't write tests unless I ask.

Stack: React + Vite with TypeScript, running in the browser, with all data in localStorage. Scaffold it with the standard Vite React TypeScript template.

Build only these features:
- [ ] Add a habit and delete a habit.
- [ ] Support multiple habits at once.
- [ ] Daily check-off: mark each habit done for today.
- [ ] Streak counter per habit.
- [ ] Simple 30-day history per habit.

The app is dark mode by default. Do not build reminders or notifications. Do not build anything else beyond the list above. If you think something extra is needed, mention it in your final message instead of building it.

Leave the details I haven't specified to you (visual design, naming, exactly how a streak is counted, edge cases such as a missed day or a deleted habit). Decide, keep it simple, and list each choice in your final message.

Ask me before proceeding only if something blocks the build. Otherwise proceed, since everything here is local and reversible. Before you start, post a one-line note on what you're about to do.

Verify by running the app, not just by building it. Start the dev server and click through this flow, using a headless browser if you can drive one: add a habit, check it off today, see the streak and the 30-day history update, then reload the page and confirm the data persists. If you can't drive a browser, run `npm run build` and a type check, and tell me plainly which parts of the click-through you could not check. If a step fails, fix the cause and rerun the flow. Don't work around it.

You're done when the click-through above passes, or you've told me exactly which steps you couldn't check. Your final message gives the command to start the app, the choices you made, and a short recap of what you verified and how.
